 12m ago GOAL! Tottenham 1-0 Arsenal (Tandberg 13) 
 35m ago Spurs v Arsenal team news 
 41m ago Preamble 
 now 08.12 EDT Premier League: Aston Villa lead Manchester City heading towards half-time at Villa Park thanks to Nicolas Jackson’s early goal. You can follow that minute-by-minute with Rob Smyth.
 Aston Villa v Manchester City: Premier League – live Read more Share 2m ago 08.10 EDT Championship: A fine finish into the roof of the net from Paris Maghoma brings Norwich level against Charlton at the Valley. Meanwhile Bobby Clark has given Derby the lead at Bramall Lane, following up after Ryan Hedges hit the foot of the post.
 Share 6m ago 08.06 EDT Suzanne Wrack at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium 
 It had been a little shaky for an under-pressure Arsenal in the opening stages of a critical north London derby. They settled a little but again failed to capitalise in the final third and Spurs punished them. Some rogue passing has seen the Gunners put the ball out of play on several occasions already and Tottenham took advantage from a corner.
 The visiting team sold out their allocation of 4,000 tickets and the fans are making a lot of noise, that the Tottenham drummer has been working hard to cut across, but they really need the players in red to match their energy and at the moment that doesn’t seem to be the case.
 It was Georgia Stanway and Emily Fox that were marking scorer Cathinka Tandberg on the corner but they don’t seem to even try to jump while she does. Stanway made up for it up the other end though, picking up her goalscoring form of the international break to crash it in off the bar and settle nerves a little. Just a little.
 Share 8m ago 08.04 EDT GOAL! Tottenham 1-1 Arsenal (Stanway 17)
 Arsenal hit back! Alessia Russo picks out Georgia Stanway as she advances into the box and the ex-Bayern midfielder guides her shot on target. Lize Kop should probably do better in the Spurs goal – she palmed it into the top corner to make it look better than it was.
 View image in fullscreen Georgia Stanway equalises for Arsenal. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  08.08 EDT 10m ago 08.01 EDT What a leap from Tandberg , who is a lifelong Spurs fan. She beat several Arsenal defenders to Victoria Pelova’s corner and Misa didn’t have much chance of stopping the header.
 Share 12m ago 08.00 EDT GOAL! Tottenham 1-0 Arsenal (Tandberg 13)
 Renée Slegers’ problems are piling up and up and up. Spurs take the lead in the derby with Cathinka Tandberg rising highest at a corner and thumping a header past Misa in the Arsenal goal.
 View image in fullscreen Cathinka Tandberg puts Tottenham ahead. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  08.08 EDT 17m ago 07.54 EDT WSL: Arsenal launch their first attack into the Spurs box as Russo and Stanway combine nicely, with the midfielder stubbing a shot at Kop, who scrambles to get it clear and out for a corner. Stanway’s shot from the edge of the box is then blocked.
 Share 20m ago 07.52 EDT Championship: Oh, Lyndon Dykes. Portsmouth are level against Millwall as the striker scrambles to meet a free-kick at his near post and ends up smothering it past his own goalkeeper. 1-1.
 Share 22m ago 07.49 EDT WSL: Tottenham’s Eveliina Summanen gets a nasty early one off Olivia Smith – studs on foot. It was an accident as they fought for the ball in midfield and, well, it’s a derby. Carry on.
 Share 27m ago 07.44 EDT WSL: The teams are out at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. It’s a bit drizzly in London today after the carnage of storm Austen yesterday. Thankfully the wind has dropped, for the moment anyway.
 Spurs go into a north London derby ahead of Arsenal for the first time in WSL history.
 View image in fullscreen Arsenal and Tottenham players shake hands before kick-off. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters Share Updated at  07.56 EDT 30m ago 07.41 EDT Championship: Jenson Metcalfe has given Millwall the lead at Fratton Park after a howler from the Portsmouth keeper Nicolas Schmid, who gave the ball straight to him on the edge of the box.
 Charlton are in front against Norwich too thanks to Charlie Kelman’s lovely finish after rounding the keeper. He pulls the John Stones ‘oh my shoulder hurts’ celebration. Sheffield Utd v Derby is the other early kick-off.
 Share Updated at  07.42 EDT 35m ago 07.36 EDT Spurs v Arsenal team news
 Here are the starting XIs for the north London derby. Martin Ho makes three changes from Spurs’ 6-2 defeat to Chelsea last weekend, while Jess Naz is back on the bench after a long spell out with an ACL injury.
 Renée Slegers has made four changes from the disappointing 1-1 draw with Birmingham – Ona Batlle and Stina Blackstenius are among those to drop to the bench – and captain Kim Little misses out with injury.
 Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kop; Dijkstra, Sombath, Blakstad; Summanen, Spence; Gaupset, Pelova, Vinberg; Tandberg.
 Subs: Panengstuen, Morris, A Nilden, Naz, Holdt, M Nilden, Hanson, Gunning-Williams, Martinez.
 Arsenal (4-2-3-1): Misa; Fox, Williamson, Catley, Hinds; Cooney-Cross, Stanway; Baum, Smith, Foord, Russo.
 Subs: Van Domselaar, Borbe, Wubben-Moy, De Almeida, Batlle, Holmberg, Reuteler, Blackstenius.
 Share 41m ago 07.30 EDT Preamble
 Hello and welcome to coverage of the afternoon’s football across the UK. Later on, we’ll have the very latest from the 3pm kick-offs in the Premier League (including Arsenal v Everton), EFL and Scottish Premiership. Before then, our attention is on the north London derby in the Women’s Super League as Spurs host Arsenal at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. The teams will be emerging from the tunnel shortly, with kick-off at 12.45pm (BST).
 The Arsenal head coach, Renée Slegers, will be desperate for a result today to relieve some of the pressure on her position. The 2025 European champions have already seen their WSL title hopes all but evaporate after failing to win their last five matches. Spurs had enjoyed a decent start to the campaign but have shipped 12 goals (!) in their last two games. Tom Garry previews this one …
 double quotation mark In discussing doubts on her future Slegers has repeated her belief she can help the team. She maintained after last weekend’s draw with Birmingham that Arsenal will recover when they fix some “details and margins”. Perhaps taking on a Tottenham side who have become only the second team in history to concede six or more goals in consecutive WSL games is the perfect opportunity.
